meta.title: 02.Sentence Analysis - Advanced (C1-C2)
meta.description: A comprehensive 60-question advanced error identification test featuring complex sentence structures, nuanced vocabulary, and contexts relatable to Indonesian professionals and academics.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Seldom has the Ministry of Tourism encounter such a massive influx of international visitors, prompting an urgent revision of the visa policies.

multiErrorSegments.text: Seldom has the Ministry of Tourism

questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with Negative Adverbials. When a sentence begins with a negative adverb like 'Seldom', the subject and auxiliary verb are inverted ('has the Ministry'), and the main verb must be in the past participle form ('encountered') to form the present perfect tense.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: It is imperative that the newly formed committee in Nusantara reviews the environmental impact assessment before approving the infrastructure project.

multiErrorSegments.text: the newly formed committee in Nusantara

questions.explanation: Topic: Subjunctive Mood. After expressions of necessity or urgency like 'It is imperative that', the verb in the subordinate clause must be in the base form (subjunctive), regardless of the subject. Thus, 'review' is correct, not 'reviews'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If the tech startup had secured Series A funding last year, it would be expanding its operations to Surabaya by now.
questions.explanation: Topic: Mixed Conditionals. This sentence correctly combines a past unreal condition ('had secured') with a present unreal result ('would be expanding'). No error.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Having been extensively renovated to preserve its colonial architecture, the historic Gedung Sate now serves as the provincial governor's office.

multiErrorSegments.text: the historic Gedung Sate now serves

questions.explanation: Topic: Perfect Participle Clauses. No error. 'Having been extensively renovated' correctly functions as a perfect passive participle clause, indicating an action completed before the main clause action, with the implied subject matching the main clause subject ('Gedung Sate').

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The new regulation, pursuant to which all foreign investments must be strictly scrutinized, was introduced by the central bank last month.

multiErrorSegments.text: was introduced by the central bank

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Relative Clauses. No error. 'Pursuant to which' is a highly formal and correct relative phrase meaning 'in accordance with which', properly connecting the regulation to the scrutiny requirement.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The sheer volume of data collected from the coral reefs in Raja Ampat indicate a significant decline in marine biodiversity.
questions.explanation: Topic: Complex Subject-Verb Agreement. The true subject is the singular noun 'volume', not the plural 'data' or 'reefs'. Therefore, the verb must be singular ('indicates').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: All multinational corporations operating in Indonesia must strictly comply to the local labor laws and environmental regulations.
questions.explanation: Topic: Nuanced Prepositional Collocations. The verb 'comply' is invariably followed by the preposition 'with', not 'to'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The digital payment platform is designed not only to streamline transactions for small merchants but also enhancing financial inclusion in rural areas.

multiErrorSegments.text: The digital payment platform is designed

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Parallelism. Correlative conjunctions like 'not only... but also' must connect grammatically parallel structures. Since 'to streamline' is an infinitive, 'enhancing' must be changed to 'to enhance' or 'enhance'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The annual revenue of the Bandung-based tech startup this year is projected to be higher than the previous year.

correctAnswers: than that of the previous year.

questions.explanation: Topic: Illogical Comparisons. One must compare 'revenue' to 'revenue', not 'revenue' to 'a year'. The pronoun 'that' is required to refer back to the singular noun 'revenue'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The ancient manuscript must have been translated by a team of philologists, given the profound understanding of Old Javanese it demonstrates.
questions.explanation: Topic: Modals of Deduction. No error. 'Must have been translated' correctly expresses a logical deduction about a past action based on present evidence.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: I regret to inform you that your research grant application has been unsuccessful, but I regret saying that the decision was not easy.

correctAnswers: but I regret having to say

multiErrorSegments.text: that the decision was not easy.

questions.explanation: Topic: Gerund vs. Infinitive with Meaning Change. 'Regret + infinitive' is used for bad news. 'Regret + gerund' is for past actions. However, 'regret to say' is the standard fixed phrase for expressing sorrow about a statement, making 'regret saying' awkward and incorrect here.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The weather being favorable, the organizers decided to proceed with the outdoor cultural festival in Yogyakarta as planned.
questions.explanation: Topic: Absolute Phrases. No error. 'The weather being favorable' is a grammatically correct absolute phrase (noun + participle) that modifies the entire main clause.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The new policy aims to provide better healthcare access for the impoverished and the elderly in remote areas of Papua.

multiErrorSegments.text: The new policy aims to provide

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Article Usage. No error. 'The + adjective' (the impoverished, the elderly) correctly functions as a plural noun to refer to a specific group of people.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The comprehensive list of required documents, along with the detailed submission guidelines, were sent to all applicants yesterday.

multiErrorSegments.text: The comprehensive list of required documents,
along with the detailed submission guidelines,

questions.explanation: Topic: Complex Subject-Verb Agreement. The true subject is the singular 'list'. Intervening phrases like 'along with' do not make the subject plural, so the verb must be singular ('was').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The project was completed on time, albeit with a slightly higher budget than originally anticipated by the stakeholders.

multiErrorSegments.text: The project was completed on time,
albeit with a slightly higher budget

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Conjunctions. No error. 'Albeit' is a formal conjunction meaning 'although', and it is correctly used here to introduce a concessive phrase.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: We had the old server room completely renovated by a specialized IT firm in Jakarta to improve data security.

multiErrorSegments.text: We had the old server room
IT firm in Jakarta to improve

questions.explanation: Topic: Causative Structures. No error. 'Have + object + past participle' correctly indicates that someone else performed the action (renovated) for the subject.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The legendary artist is said that he has been working on a new masterpiece for over five years in his Bali studio.
questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Passive Voice. The structure 'Subject + is said + to-infinitive' is required here. 'That he has been working' is incorrect; it must be 'to have been working'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The investors are eagerly waiting to know what is the primary reason for the sudden delay in the infrastructure project.

multiErrorSegments.text: to know what is the primary reason
correctAnswers: to know what the primary reason is

questions.explanation: Topic: Indirect Question Word Order. In an embedded or indirect question, the word order must be subject + verb ('what the primary reason is'), not verb + subject ('what is the primary reason').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The new software update has significantly improved the user interface, making it more intuitive for elderly users.
questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Adverb Placement & Participles. No error. The mid-position adverb 'significantly' is correctly placed between the auxiliary 'has' and the main verb 'improved'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The average temperature in Bandung during the rainy season is significantly lower than Jakarta.
questions.explanation: Topic: Illogical Comparisons. You must compare 'temperature' to 'temperature', not 'temperature' to a city. Use 'that of' to refer back to the singular noun 'temperature'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Based on the manager's vague statements during the meeting, we can imply that the company will be downsizing its workforce soon.

multiErrorSegments.text: Based on the manager's vague statements
during the meeting, we can imply
correctAnswers: during the meeting, we can infer

multiErrorSegments.text: that the company will be downsizing

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Vocabulary (Imply vs. Infer). Speakers or writers 'imply' (suggest), while listeners or readers 'infer' (deduce). Since 'we' are the listeners, 'infer' is correct.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Please revert back to the client as soon as possible with the updated project proposal and the revised budget.

multiErrorSegments.text: to the client as soon as possible

questions.explanation: Topic: Redundancy and Pleonasm. 'Revert' already means 'to go back' or 'to reply'. Adding 'back' is redundant. Use 'revert to' or 'get back to'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The local artisans, which have been practicing their craft for generations, are struggling to compete with mass-produced goods.
questions.explanation: Topic: Restrictive vs. Non-restrictive Relative Clauses. When referring to people ('artisans'), the relative pronoun 'who' must be used, not 'which'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Only after the board of directors reviewed the financial audit did they realize the extent of the discrepancies.

multiErrorSegments.text: Only after the board of directors

questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with 'Only after'. No error. When a sentence begins with 'Only after' + clause, the main clause requires subject-auxiliary inversion ('did they realize').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Had the logistics team known about the port strike, they would have routed the shipment through a different harbor.

multiErrorSegments.text: they would have routed the shipment

questions.explanation: Topic: Conditional Inversion. No error. 'Had the logistics team known' is a correct and formal inversion of 'If the logistics team had known' (Third Conditional).

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Despite the economic downturn, a large number of new startups have emerged in Jakarta, bringing a great deal of innovation to the market.

multiErrorSegments.text: a large number of new startups
bringing a great deal of innovation

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Quantifiers. No error. 'A large number of' correctly modifies the countable noun 'startups' (taking a plural verb), and 'a great deal of' correctly modifies the uncountable noun 'innovation'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: It is high time that the local government takes decisive action to address the worsening air pollution in the city.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subjunctive in 'It is high time'. This expression is always followed by a past simple verb to indicate that something should have been done already ('took', not 'takes').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The manager in charge of the regional sales division will be presenting the quarterly results tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Topic: Prepositional Phrases as Adjectives. No error. 'In charge of the regional sales division' correctly functions as an adjectival phrase modifying 'The manager'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The new policy will only affect employees who have been with the company for less than two years.

multiErrorSegments.text: who have been with the company

questions.explanation: Topic: Misplaced Modifiers. The adverb 'only' should be placed immediately before the word or phrase it modifies. Placing it before 'affect' suggests the policy will do nothing else but affect them, whereas 'affect only employees' correctly limits the scope of who is affected.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The recent archaeological discovery in East Java has casted serious doubt on the previously accepted timeline of the Majapahit Empire.
questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Collocations & Irregular Verbs. The past participle of 'cast' is 'cast', not 'casted'. The correct collocation is 'cast doubt on'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The system failure was caused by a sudden power outage, not by a software malfunction.
questions.explanation: Topic: Noun Adjuncts. No error. 'System' and 'software' correctly function as noun adjuncts (nouns modifying other nouns) to specify the type of failure and malfunction.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The initial test results were promising; however, the subsequent trials failed to replicate the same level of efficiency.

multiErrorSegments.text: The initial test results were promising;

questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctive Adverb Punctuation. No error. The semicolon before 'however' and the comma after it are correctly used to join two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: As it was expected by the market analysts, the central bank decided to keep the interest rates unchanged this quarter.

multiErrorSegments.text: the central bank decided to keep
the interest rates unchanged this quarter.

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Use of 'As'. In this formal construction, 'As' acts as a relative pronoun referring to the entire main clause. The dummy subject 'it' is unnecessary and incorrect; 'As was expected' is the standard form.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Such was the impact of the new e-commerce regulation that several small vendors had to temporarily halt their operations.

multiErrorSegments.text: that several small vendors had to

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced 'Such... that' Structures. No error. Inverting the sentence to 'Such was the impact... that...' is a correct and highly formal way to emphasize the degree of the impact.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The safety officer emphasized the strict protocols lest an accident occurs during the factory inspection.

multiErrorSegments.text: the strict protocols lest an accident

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Lest' Constructions. The conjunction 'lest' (meaning 'for fear that') is always followed by the subjunctive mood, which uses the base form of the verb ('occur'), not the third-person singular ('occurs').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If only I have invested in that property in South Jakarta five years ago, I would be financially secure now.

multiErrorSegments.text: in South Jakarta five years ago,
I would be financially secure now.

questions.explanation: Topic: 'If only' for Past Regrets. To express regret about a past situation, 'if only' must be followed by the past perfect tense ('had invested'), not the present perfect.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: I would rather you did not disclose the confidential merger details to anyone outside the executive team.

multiErrorSegments.text: you did not disclose the confidential

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced 'Would rather'. When 'would rather' is followed by a different subject ('you'), the verb must be in the past subjunctive ('did not disclose') to refer to a present or future preference.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Supposing the heavy rainfall continues throughout the week, the agricultural committee will declare a state of emergency.
questions.explanation: Topic: 'Supposing' Conditionals. No error. 'Supposing' functions identically to 'if' in conditional sentences and is correctly followed by the present simple tense for a real future possibility.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Although the heavy monsoon rains, the construction of the new toll road in Sumatra proceeded according to schedule.

correctAnswers: Although there were heavy monsoon rains,

multiErrorSegments.text: the construction of the new toll road

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Despite' vs. 'Although'. 'Although' is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb). Since 'the heavy monsoon rains' is a noun phrase, the preposition 'Despite' must be used.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: After living in Singapore for three months, she is finally getting used to the fast-paced lifestyle and the humid weather.

multiErrorSegments.text: for three months, she is finally

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Get used to'. No error. 'Getting used to' correctly describes the process of becoming accustomed to something, and it is properly followed by noun phrases.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Need the board of directors to approve the budget before we can proceed with the hiring process?

correctAnswers: Does the board of directors need

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Need' as a Main Verb vs. Semi-modal. In modern English, 'need' is rarely used as a semi-modal in standard interrogative sentences without 'do' support. 'Does... need' is the correct standard interrogative form.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The committee decided to invest in renewable energy sources rather than to continue relying on fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: Topic: 'Rather than' Parallelism. When 'rather than' is used to contrast two infinitive actions, the 'to' is typically omitted in the second part to maintain smooth parallelism ('to invest... rather than continue').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: He speaks about the ancient maritime trade routes as if he were a historian who had dedicated his entire life to the subject.

multiErrorSegments.text: He speaks about the ancient maritime
trade routes as if he were
his entire life to the subject.

questions.explanation: Topic: 'As if' Subjunctive. No error. 'As if he were' correctly uses the past subjunctive to describe a hypothetical or unreal comparison in the present.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Provided that the necessary permits are obtained, the construction of the new eco-resort will commence next month.

multiErrorSegments.text: of the new eco-resort will commence

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Provided that' Conditionals. No error. 'Provided that' is a formal conjunction meaning 'on the condition that', and it is correctly followed by a present tense verb in a first conditional structure.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: No sooner the meeting had concluded than the journalists began asking the CEO about the sudden resignation.

multiErrorSegments.text: the journalists began asking the CEO

questions.explanation: Topic: 'No sooner... than' Inversion. When a sentence begins with 'No sooner', the subject and auxiliary verb must be inverted ('had the meeting concluded').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Not until the final data analysis was completed did the researchers fully understand the implications of their findings.

multiErrorSegments.text: Not until the final data analysis

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Not until' Inversion. No error. The sentence correctly uses inversion in the main clause ('did the researchers fully understand') after a fronted 'Not until' phrase.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Seldom we see such a high level of dedication and professionalism from the volunteer team in rural areas.

multiErrorSegments.text: we see such a high level
correctAnswers: do we see such a high level

multiErrorSegments.text: from the volunteer team in rural areas.

questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with Negative Adverbs. Fronted negative or restrictive adverbs like 'Seldom' require subject-auxiliary inversion in the main clause ('do we see').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Under no circumstances the confidential client data should be shared with external parties without explicit written consent.

multiErrorSegments.text: the confidential client data should be
correctAnswers: should the confidential client data be

questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with 'Under no circumstances'. This negative phrase at the beginning of a sentence mandates subject-auxiliary inversion ('should the data be').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: On no account are visitors permitted to enter the restricted archaeological zone without an authorized guide.
questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with 'On no account'. No error. The sentence correctly applies subject-auxiliary inversion ('are visitors') after the fronted negative phrase 'On no account'.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: Little did the early investors know that the small startup would eventually become a unicorn in the Southeast Asian market.

multiErrorSegments.text: Little did the early investors know
that the small startup would eventually
become a unicorn in the Southeast

questions.explanation: Topic: Inversion with 'Little'. No error. 'Little did [subject] know' is a correct and idiomatic inverted structure used to emphasize that someone was completely unaware of something.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If the shipment should gets delayed due to the typhoon, please notify the logistics team immediately.

multiErrorSegments.text: gets delayed due to the typhoon,
correctAnswers: get delayed due to the typhoon,

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Should' in Conditional Clauses. After the modal verb 'should', the base form of the verb must be used ('get'), not the third-person singular ('gets').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Were the proposed merger to be approved by the regulatory body, it would create the largest telecommunications company in the region.

multiErrorSegments.text: Were the proposed merger to be

questions.explanation: Topic: 'Were' in Conditional Clauses. No error. 'Were [subject] to [verb]' is a correct and highly formal inversion of 'If [subject] were to [verb]' (Second Conditional).

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The success of the new fintech startup in Jakarta is largely independent from the global economic fluctuations.

multiErrorSegments.text: The success of the new fintech startup
in Jakarta is largely independent from
correctAnswers: in Jakarta is largely independent of

questions.explanation: Topic: Advanced Prepositional Collocations. The adjective 'independent' is correctly followed by the preposition 'of', not 'from'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: What makes the Komodo dragon truly fascinating is not its size, but its unique venomous bite.

multiErrorSegments.text: truly fascinating is not its size,

questions.explanation: Topic: Cleft Sentences for Emphasis. No error. The 'What... is...' structure correctly emphasizes the subject complement, and the parallelism 'not its size, but its... bite' is grammatically sound.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The socioeconomic disparity in the region is becoming progressively more exacerbated by the lack of equitable educational opportunities.

multiErrorSegments.text: The socioeconomic disparity in the region
by the lack of equitable educational

questions.explanation: Topic: Double Comparatives / Redundancy. 'Exacerbated' is already a comparative concept in this context (made worse). Adding 'more' is redundant and grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The ministry received a plethora of misinformation and numerous equipments regarding the new agricultural subsidy program.

multiErrorSegments.text: The ministry received a plethora of

correctAnswers: misinformation and numerous pieces of equipment

questions.explanation: Topic: Uncountable Nouns. 'Equipment' is strictly uncountable in English and cannot be pluralized with an 's'. It must be quantified as 'pieces of equipment' or 'items of equipment'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Should the monsoon rains exacerbate the existing flooding, the municipal government will invoke emergency protocols.
questions.explanation: Topic: Inverted First Conditional. No error. 'Should + subject + base verb' is a formal and correct inversion of 'If + subject + present simple' for real future possibilities.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The consortium looks forward to spearheading the initiative and fostering sustainable development across the archipelago.
questions.explanation: Topic: 'Look forward to' + Gerund. No error. The phrase 'look forward to' requires a gerund because 'to' functions as a preposition here. 'Spearheading' and 'fostering' are correctly parallel.

questions.question: Click on error(s) and type correction.
questions.sentence: The intricate batik motifs were meticulously hand-drawn and subsequently imbued with symbolic meaning by the artisans.
questions.explanation: Topic: Passive Voice Parallelism. No error. The sentence correctly maintains parallel structure in the passive voice ('were... hand-drawn and subsequently imbued').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Rendang is frequently cited by culinary experts as one of the most exquisite culinary masterpiece in the world.

multiErrorSegments.text: culinary experts as one of the

questions.explanation: Topic: Superlative + Plural Noun. The structure 'one of the' must always be followed by a plural noun ('masterpieces'), as it refers to a single item within a larger group.
